title: Carabao Cup Fourth Round Predictions: Liverpool Host Chelsea, Man City Face Brighton
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackOct 26, 2026There’s an array of all-Premier League clashes this week in the Carabao Cup fourth round. / Paul Currie/AFP/Getty Images (Liverpool duo); Carl Recine/Getty Images (Haaland)While the Champions League and the rest of UEFA’s club competitions enjoy a week off, there’s domestic cup action to watch, with several of the Premier League’s top dogs taking center stage.

We’re in the midst of an unrelenting period up until the November international break, and plenty of those teams with European commitments remain keen to enjoy a cup run and have supporters dreaming of a Wembley day out.

13 of the 16 teams that remain in the Carabao Cup ply their trade in the top-flight, so there‘s an array of all-Premier League affairs to enjoy midweek, including a couple of potentially tantalizing tussles.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts the Carabao Cup fourth round to play out.

Arsenal visit League Two Fleetwood. / Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesPrediction: Fleetwood 0–3 Arsenal

Arsenal were the big winners of the Premier League weekend, even if their fiercest rivals secured a rare victory at Stamford Bridge. The Gunners moved level on points with Manchester City at the division’s summit after easing to a 2–0 win against Everton and seeing the Cityzens beaten at Villa Park.
Mikel Arteta will undoubtedly have one eye cast on Sunday‘s trip to Anfield, where the Gunners have a wretched record, and he’ll have the chance to preserve key roster members at Highbury on Tuesday.

No, Arsenal aren’t traveling back in time to their old stomping grounds. Rather, they’re facing Fleetwood Town for the very first time. The Fishermen reached the fourth round for the first time in their history by beating Sheffield United last month, but their form has fallen off a cliff since.
Five defeats from their previous seven league outings mean Mark Lawlor’s men sit 18th in League Two.
Anything but a convincing away victory would be a surprise.
The Cityzens were beaten in the Premier League for the first time this season at the weekend. /  Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesPrediction: Man City 2–1 Brighton
There’s a ‘Big Six’ affair at Anfield slightly later in the evening, yet this may be the most intriguing tie of the round.

Both teams entered the Premier League weekend in red-hot form, but were both stopped in their tracks. Man City were undone by a Nicolas Jackson brace at Saturday lunchtime, meaning their winning streak to start the league season was snapped. It left Chelsea’s record of nine straight wins to begin their title defense in 2005–06 intact.

Brighton & Hove Albion, meanwhile, were made to rue missed chances on Merseyside, as two quick-fire Liverpool goals meant the Seagulls fell to a 2–0 defeat. Despite the shutout, Brighton remain the league’s top scorers, and they’re aiming to complete a Manchester double at the start of their Carabao Cup campaign.
Brighton rallied from a 2–0 deficit to beat Manchester United 3–2 in round three, while City thumped Norwich City at the start of their trophy defense.
Bournemouth manager Marco Rose is enjoying the team’s recent hot streak. / Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty ImagesPrediction: Bournemouth 3–1 Aston Villa
Bournemouth and Aston Villa probably don’t mind games arriving thick and fast at the moment, given their respective moods.

The Cherries had quite the week, thrashing two mammoth insitutions in AC Milan and Manchester United in back-to-back games. Marco Rose’s men remain perfect in Europe and showcased at the weekend why any early-season panic was unfounded.

Villa, though, are equally buoyant. Unai Emery is at it again, folks. Just when you thought a rebuild was beyond him, he reminds everyone why he’s one of the most revered coaches in the sport. Villa’s wretched start to the campaign is a distant memory, and they travel down to the south coast on a four-game winning run.
